To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the recognition of bed bugs in a sample of four German cities was low, (2) the knowledge of the presence of bed bug in a household or apartment was even lower, (3) the knowledge of bed bugs was associated with previous encounters with bed bugs, and (4) people who heard about bed bugs from the mass media showed reduced recognition rates of bed bug images.
13% (95% confidence interval 11-16%) of a sample of four large German cities recognized a bed bug, and 15% (95% CI 12-19%) would call a pest control company in case of an early-stage infestation.

1) the ability of people to recognize bed bugs is low; 2) the ability of recognizing bed bugs is higher if people had previous contacts with bedbugs or if they heard about bedbugs from friends or relatives or in school; 3) people who heard about bed bugs in print media, television or the internet showed a lower ability to recognize bedbugs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the human side of bed bugs and the human side of their control.
the question of why bed bugs are feared and what people would do in case of a bed bug infestation.
people’s ability to identify bed bugs and the reasons for this ability or inability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bed bug is not well known in the general German population and that the majority of people would not call for help if they encountered a bed bug infestation.
the bed bug is not yet well understood by most people, and this lack of understanding could have a negative impact on the effectiveness of control measures.
bed bugs are a problem for the few and not the majority of the population, but that the majority of people do not have the necessary skills to deal with the few who are affected.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the majority of people are unprepared to deal with an early stage bed bug infestation.
bed bugs are a threat to the health, hygiene and well-being of the population.
the majority of the German population is unaware of the bed bug, but that a small minority is well prepared.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bed bug control will not be successful if the people affected are not prepared to deal with the problem.
people’s knowledge about the bed bug is limited.
the public is not prepared to deal with bed bugs.
